declared_deviations.rule: agent_profile/protocol.md §10 — 'Schema Draft 2020-12 dùng oneOf discriminated type'
declared_deviations.deviation: Schema này dùng `allOf` gồm bảy nhánh `if/then` thay vì `oneOf`.
declared_deviations.reason: Bảy nhánh ở đây KHÔNG phải một union phân biệt theo `type`: chúng là các ràng buộc CÓ ĐIỀU KIỆN trên cùng MỘT loại đối tượng (result=NOT_APPLICABLE ⇒ bắt buộc not_applicable_reason; execution.kind=command ⇒ bắt buộc command; review_type=SELF_VALIDATION ⇒ giới hạn claim.supports_label). Một manifest phải thoả TẤT CẢ các điều kiện áp dụng cho nó, không phải đúng một trong bảy. Diễn đạt bằng `oneOf` sẽ sai về ngữ nghĩa: một bản ghi vừa NOT_APPLICABLE vừa có execution.kind=not_executed sẽ khớp hai nhánh và bị `oneOf` từ chối. Đối tượng vẫn đóng kín: additionalProperties=false ở mọi object definition.

checks.title: Fixtures that declare a JSON Schema validation target validate (or fail) as declared
checks.oracle: expected_validation 'accept' => every payload validates; 'reject'/'reject_schema' => the negative payload raises at least one error; 'reject_semantic' => the payload validates (rejection is a downstream semantic gate, SRC-PLAN §10); 'not_applicable' => skipped with a reason. A validation_target that is not a *.schema.json path is a contract reference, not a schema, and is NOT_APPLICABLE.

checks.title: Operation-shaped tokens in prose resolve against contracts/ports.yaml
checks.oracle: Single source of the rule: contracts/ports.yaml conventions.prose_token_rule_vi. A backticked `<a>.<b>` must resolve to an operation of ports.yaml OR an entity.column of entities.yaml; tokens whose first segment is neither a known operation domain nor a known entity name (file paths, YAML structural keys, hosts, library idioms) are ignored. This check reports the operation half. E0-04 reads structured fields only; this reaches the sentences, where F-A2R1-01 lived.

checks.title: Column-shaped tokens in prose resolve against contracts/data/entities.yaml
checks.oracle: Single source of the rule: contracts/ports.yaml conventions.prose_token_rule_vi. This check reports the column half. Splitting it out of E0-04b (ruling FIX7) keeps 'someone named an operation that does not exist' distinct from 'someone named a column that does not exist' — different owners, different fixes.

checks.title: Error-code-shaped tokens in prose are registered codes or listed vocabulary
checks.oracle: A backticked SCREAMING_SNAKE token must be a code in contracts/errors.yaml or a word in the tool's STATUS_VOCABULARY — which covers the baseline §3 status/claim vocabularies and the protocol.md message types (Coordinator ruling, FIX7 wave). This is how F-A2R1-06 (SAVE_ALREADY_EXISTS) was found.

checks.title: Every contract / schema / fixture / registry file carries the baseline §3 header
checks.oracle: YAML: the 14 fields are top-level keys. Markdown: they are in the YAML front-matter. JSON Schema: $id/title/description plus an x-contract object. Fixture JSON: an x-contract object or the directory README lists the file (ruling in baseline §3). ADRs use the R-05 field set instead.

checks.title: State machines: closed state enums, reachability, terminal states have no outgoing rows
checks.oracle: every token in a transition from/to resolves to a value of that file's primary state enum (alternatives separated by '|' are split; trailing parentheticals are commentary; a creation sentinel means the row is created); every state listed as terminal or non-terminal is reachable from the initial state; a terminal state has no outgoing transition unless the file names that transition in terminal_state_rule; the terminal / non-terminal / quasi-terminal lists partition the enum.

checks.title: Every forbidden edge in contracts/modules.yaml is covered by a scenario
checks.oracle: for each forbidden_edges[].id there is a scenario in acceptance/scenarios.yaml whose forbidden_edge_refs contains it

checks.title: Forbidden edge ↔ denied case ↔ boundary fixture event is a content-matching bijection
checks.oracle: For each forbidden_edges[] entry: exactly ONE denied_cases[] entry references it, and that entry's attempted_edge.caller/callee equal the edge's caller/callee and its expected_error_code is a registered code; AND exactly ONE event in the boundary sweep fixture references it, with actor == caller, callee == callee, denied_case_ref == that case's id, the same expected_error_code, and (when it names an operation) the same operation. A named operation must be OWNED BY the callee when the callee is a MOD-* module (F-A2R1-05); when the callee is an EXT-* system it names the internal port whose effect is attempted, per the convention declared in modules.yaml default_deny. Nothing may reference an unknown edge, and nothing may be referenced twice. Presence of a pinned case is NOT sufficient (CR-PC01-11).
notes: bijection checked over 36 forbidden edges, 36 denied cases, 36 sweep events

checks.title: No P0 requirement with status XN or UQ is an ORPHAN in acceptance/traceability.csv
checks.oracle: traceability.csv has one row per requirements.csv row and no row with priority==P0 and status in {XN, UQ} carries coverage_status == ORPHAN

checks.title: Every invariant has a dedicated positive scenario AND a dedicated negative scenario
checks.oracle: for each invariant id, acceptance/scenarios.yaml contains at least one scenario citing it declared polarity 'positive' and at least one declared 'negative'. Ruling F-A2R1-10: 'mixed' counts for NEITHER pole — a combined scenario is not a dedicated counterexample, and the check must not claim more than its oracle delivers.

checks.title: No asserted TBD, no status CLOSED/ACCEPTED, no claim above DRAFT_FOR_REVIEW
checks.oracle: structured fields: `status`/`claim_ceiling`/`completion_claim` values are checked exactly. Free text: occurrences are reported when the line carries no negation and no vocabulary context.

checks.title: Coverage windows in reporting fixtures are half-open and contiguous
checks.oracle: for every fixture that carries coverage_window rows: window_from < window_to for each row, and for consecutive sequence numbers window_to[n] == window_from[n+1] (no gap, no overlap)

checks.title: Every fixture event names an allowed caller of the operation (rulings R-02, R4-02)
checks.oracle: events[].actor is in ports.yaml caller_modules for events[].operation AND the triple (actor, owner_module, operation) is in modules.yaml allowed_edges. `performed_by` is the executing service and is never read as a caller assertion. An event marked `edge_assertion: forbidden` asserts the opposite: the triple must be ABSENT from allowed_edges and the fixture must expect one of UNAUTHORIZED / FORBIDDEN_EDGE / CAPABILITY_DENIED. An event that carries an actor but no recognised operation key fails loudly rather than being skipped (F-A1R3-02).

checks.title: Every column named in given.rows and expected.rows exists in entities.yaml (R4-01)
checks.oracle: for each table name under given.rows / expected.rows, every object key is either (a) a declared field of that entity in contracts/data/entities.yaml, (b) an annotation whose key starts with '_', or (c) a column carrying an in-file `pending_cr: CR-…` marker. No per-package allowlist (ruling R4-01).

limitations: E0 only. Nothing here proves that any code exists or that any guard runs (SRC-PLAN §14.2).
Reference checks find dangling references, not missing ones: a relationship nobody wrote down cannot be detected.
No OpenAPI 3.1 validator is installed in this environment, so contracts/http/openapi.yaml is checked only as YAML plus reference integrity.
Fixture semantics are read, not executed. A fixture that parses and whose columns resolve is not a passing test.
The free-text half of E0-12 is heuristic: it reports lines and a human must read them; it can over-report.
